title: Tesla on Autopilot stops on the I-75 shoulder at Sarasota with a drunk driver asleep; Florida police charge the 37-year-old with DUI
summary: Ouest-France (3 May 2026, citing ABC 7): around 2 a.m. on 24 Apr 2026 police found a 37-year-old woman unconscious in her stopped Tesla on Interstate 75; blood alcohol over twice the limit; charged...
account: Alexandre Chauvel reported in Ouest-France on 3 May 2026, relaying the Sarasota station ABC 7, on a car stopped on Interstate 75. Officers were alerted at about 2 a.m. on Friday 24 April 2026 to a car on the emergency lane at Sarasota, Florida. They found a 37-year-old woman unconscious at the wheel of a Tesla. Local police, quoted without naming the agency or officer, said she should not have been driving. They said her blood alcohol was more than twice the legal limit. They said she had assumed the Tesla would bring her home safely on Autopilot. The article explains that cabin sensors check that the driver is looking ahead and warn them. If the driver does not reopen their eyes after the first warning, the vehicle stops. She was arrested and is being prosecuted for driving under the influence. The Tesla model is not stated. Neither a police report nor the ABC 7 story is among the sources. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the event as a protective response with French-language sources.
purpose: Autopilot's driver-attention monitoring is built to warn an inattentive driver. It brings the car to a stop if the driver does not respond. It is not designed to drive an impaired person home.
system: Tesla Autopilot with cabin driver-attention monitoring (model not stated)

ratings.reason: An unconscious, intoxicated driver came to a stop without a crash. The sources document no injury and no collision avoided.
Other road users were exposed to a stationary car on the shoulder rather than a moving one. No incident with them is documented.

ai_role.statement: Per the report, the attention-monitoring logic issued warnings and then stopped the vehicle on the emergency lane. The agency, the vehicle data and the duration of the stop are not given. The police framed the episode as misuse rather than a rescue.
